parameters.query: SELECT vb.booking_id, vb.engagement_id, vb.vendor_id, vb.service_type, vb.cost, v.vendor_name, v.rating, e.industry, e.engagement_name, e.budget_variance, c.client_name FROM AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDOR_BOOKINGS vb JOIN AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDORS v ON v.vendor_id = vb.vendor_id JOIN AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.ENGAGEMENTS e ON e.engagement_id = vb.engagement_id JOIN AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.CLIENTS c ON c.client_id = e.client_id WHERE vb.status = 'CONFIRMED' AND vb.replaced_booking_id IS NULL AND c.source = 'DEMO_LIVE' AND e.status = 'IN_PROGRESS' AND ('{{ $json.body?.engagement_id ?? "" }}' = '' OR vb.engagement_id = '{{ $json.body?.engagement_id ?? "" }}') ORDER BY vb.booked_at DESC LIMIT 1
UPDATE AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDOR_BOOKINGS SET status = 'DECLINED' WHERE booking_id = '{{ $('Find Live Booking').first().json.BOOKING_ID }}'

SELECT v.vendor_id, v.vendor_name, v.rating, v.cost_per_unit, v.capacity FROM AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDORS v WHERE v.industry = '{{ $('Find Live Booking').first().json.INDUSTRY }}' AND v.service_type = '{{ $('Find Live Booking').first().json.SERVICE_TYPE }}' AND v.active = TRUE AND v.vendor_id <> '{{ $('Find Live Booking').first().json.VENDOR_ID }}' ORDER BY v.rating DESC, v.cost_per_unit ASC LIMIT 5

values.content:
=A confirmed vendor has just withdrawn and must be replaced now. Choose the best replacement and explain the decision.

(Context for your judgement only, and never to be repeated in your answer: this is happening overnight with no staff available, so your choice stands as the decision of record.)

Engagement: {{ $json.engagement_name }} ({{ $json.client_name }})
Service needed: {{ $json.service_type }}
Vendor that withdrew: {{ $json.declined_vendor }} -- rating {{ $json.declined_rating }}, ${{ $json.declined_cost }} per unit
Current budget variance on this engagement: ${{ $json.budget_variance }}

Available alternatives:
{{ $json.candidates }}

Return ONLY valid JSON with these exact keys:
  chosen_vendor_id      the id of the vendor you are booking
  chosen_vendor_name    its name
  chosen_cost           its cost per unit, as a plain number
  budget_impact         chosen_cost minus the withdrawn vendor's cost, as a plain number (negative means a saving)
  reasoning             TWO OR THREE SENTENCES in plain business language
  alternatives_considered  one sentence naming the other candidates and why each was not chosen
  confidence            a number between 0 and 1

RULES FOR reasoning -- this text is stored on the engagement record and projected in front of senior executives:
- Write as an operations manager briefing a client, not as an AI describing itself.
- Never say "I", "as an AI", "the model", "based on the data provided", or "optimal".
- Never mention the time of day, that nobody was available, or that no human was involved. Do not praise the speed or the automation. That is the presenter's line, not the record's.
- Name the tradeoff in money and service terms. Say what it costs and what it protects.
- Describe service, not database fields: write "enough capacity to cover the engagement", never "180-unit capacity".
- No bullet points, no headings, no preamble. Just the sentences.

nodes.name: Request Approval
nodes.notes: Starts the Nintex component workflow. The token is a QUERY parameter, not a header -- it lives in the 'Nintex Approval Start' Query Auth credential so it never sits in this node. Returns HTTP 202 with a BARE INSTANCE ID AS PLAIN TEXT, not JSON, hence responseFormat text.

nodes.name: Wait for Decision
nodes.notes: 3s between polls. Also the loop target: 'Timed Out?' false routes back here.

nodes.name: Poll Task

parameters.notes: status=all IS LOAD BEARING. Without it this endpoint defaults to status=active, and a task that has just been approved or rejected drops out of the response entirely -- 0 tasks, outcome forever null, guaranteed timeout no matter how fast the human taps. v2, not v1: /workflows/v1/tasks returns 404. Uses the OAuth2 client-credentials credential because read:task is granted there and the minted start token is rejected by this endpoint.

nodes.notes: v2, not v1 -- /workflows/v1/tasks returns 404. Uses the OAuth2 client-credentials credential because read:task is granted there and the minted start token is rejected by this endpoint.

nodes.name: Evaluate Poll
nodes.notes: outcome is null while the task is active -- that null is the poll condition. Bounded at 20 attempts (~60s) so a demo cannot hang.

nodes.name: Timed Out?
nodes.notes: False routes back to Wait for Decision. This is the poll loop.

nodes.name: Mark Reviewed
nodes.notes: Flips human_reviewed on the decision row. This is the audit trail answering 'so the AI just does whatever it wants?'

nodes.name: Book Fallback
nodes.notes: Next-ranked vendor chosen in SQL, not by a second agent call. A wrong tap on stage must recover in one step.

nodes.name: Timeout Summary
nodes.notes: Deliberately does NOT confirm the booking. Timing out and proceeding anyway would make the governance beat a lie.

nodes.name: Read Fallback

parameters.query: =SELECT v.vendor_name, b.cost FROM AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDOR_BOOKINGS b JOIN AIGS_DEMO.ONBOARDING.VENDORS v ON v.vendor_id = b.vendor_id WHERE b.booking_id = '{{ $('Apply Decision').first().json.fallback_booking_id }}'

nodes.notes: The fallback vendor is chosen inside SQL, so its name and cost are only knowable after the insert. Read them back rather than concatenating them in SQL.

nodes.name: Build Fallback Decision
nodes.notes: Builds a plain INSERT ... VALUES. Deliberately no || concatenation and no TO_VARCHAR format model: that version compiled fine when run directly against Snowflake but failed inside an n8n expression, and a live demo is the wrong place to find out why.

nodes.name: Mark Reviewed After Reject
nodes.notes: A rejection IS a human review. Without this the original decision row reads human_reviewed = FALSE on the audit panel, which undercuts the whole governance beat. Same statement as the approve path.

activeVersion.name: Mark the original decision reviewed on the reject path too
activeVersion.description: After a rejection the original VENDOR_DECLINED decision row was left human_reviewed = FALSE, even though a human had reviewed it and said no. On the audit panel that reads as unreviewed, which is the opposite of the point the beat makes. Reuses the same sql_reviewed statement already proven on the approve path.
